articles.title: Quevin Castro cause of death: former West Bromwich Albion player dies during a match in Portugal at age 25
articles.standfirst: He felt unwell at the start of the training match against Estrela da Amadora
articles.summary: He felt unwell at the start of the training match against Estrela da Amadora
articles.body:
"The Portuguese footballer Quévin Castro, former West Bromwich player , died at the age of 25 while playing in a preparatory match between his club, Real Sport Clube, from Portugal's amateur divisions, and Estrela da Amadora.

In a statement, Real Sport Club confirmed the death of its player and expressed its " deep sadness and immense sorrow " over the death of the midfielder, who throughout his brief career had come through Chelsea's youth ranks.

" Quevin Castro was much more than a player, he was an integral part of our family and has left an indelible mark on all those who knew him, both on and off the field," wrote the club from the city of Massamá, on the outskirts of Lisbon.

According to the Portuguese press, Castro felt unwell at the start of the training match against Estrela da Amadora , was treated on the pitch with a defibrillator and subsequently transferred to the hospital, where his death was confirmed.

Castro spent most of his career in English football , where he played for historic clubs such as West Bromwich Albion, Notts County and Chelsea's under-23s, and this season he had returned to Portuguese football to play for Real Sport Clube.

articles.title: From playing in Champions League finals to waiting for a call: the stars who are still free agents
articles.standfirst: The transfer market is entering its final stretch and there are still footballers with a brilliant past who have not found a destination. Some were protagonists on Europe’s biggest stages.
articles.summary: The transfer market is entering its final stretch and there are still footballers with a brilliant past who have not found a destination. Some were protagonists on Europe’s biggest stages.
articles.body:
There are images that seem hard to imagine in modern football. Star footballers at Real Madrid, Bayern, Liverpool, Manchester City and other European giants are searching for an opportunity, but the market moves on and their next destinations are still unknown.

They are not little-known names. They are champions and key figures in the most important story in European football. There are several stars who are without a contract and can sign for a club at any time.

For years they were familiar names in the lineups of the continent’s biggest clubs. They won titles, played in finals, and were key figures for their teams, but now they are going through an unexpected situation: they are still without a contract.

Some names that appear are: S ergio Ramos, Dani Carvajal, James Rodríguez, David Alaba, Leon Goretzka, Philippe Coutinho, Fabinho, Georginio Wijnaldum and Riyad Mahrez.

Their achievements and careers speak for themselves, but the market does not always operate according to what has been accomplished. Even footballers with Champions experience can end up waiting until the final days of the transfer window to learn their next destination. All of them have behind them a career marked by great moments. They have played on the most demanding stages, shared a dressing room with some of the biggest stars on the planet, and lifted trophies that are part of the recent history of football.

One of the most notable cases is Paul Pogba . The French midfielder terminated his contract with Monaco last August 19 due to the lack of playing time last season, although his future seems closer to a club in the MLS .

The countdown has already begun

As the transfer window draws ever closer to closing, the future of these stars remains uncertain. Some may be hoping for a major offer, while others will have to adapt to new conditions to find a new destination.

Age, physical condition, salary, and long-term planning are factors that can hinder deals even with footballers of enormous quality.

The Turkish and South American teams are the ones most linked with the possible signings of these players. The question is which club will decide to bet on players who still have a lot to offer.

articles.title: A Bitter Debut for Jorge Campos' Son in Canada: A Serious Mistake That Led to a Goal After an Impressive Start
articles.standfirst: The Campos surname returns between the posts: Kai Antonio makes his professional debut and makes the best save of the game, though a blooper took some of the shine off his performance.
articles.summary: The Campos surname returns between the posts: Kai Antonio makes his professional debut and makes the best save of the game, though a blooper took some of the shine off his performance.
articles.body:
Kai Antonio Campos had a professional debut marked by mixed emotions. The goalkeeper started for Inter Toronto against Forge FC and showed quick reflexes to make one of the best saves of the match; however, in the second half, he was at fault for the tying goal after being beaten by a header.

At just 20 years old, the young goalkeeper had to rise to the demands of professional soccer in his first game, shining in one of the match’s most memorable moments while also taking a hard hit on the goal he conceded.

The Save That Defined His Debut

The play came during the match against Forge. Kai Antonio Campos initially stopped a shot by Kyle Bekker , and although the rebound fell to the forward, he reacted immediately to deny the forward’s second attempt, making a double save to keep the ball out of his net.

The play ended in a corner kick, and the Canadian Premier League recognized it as the “Save of the Match,” making that save one of the highlights of his first appearance as a professional. The award confirmed that, despite the result, the rookie’s performance was worthy of recognition.

Minutes later, the less pleasant side of his debut emerged. Forge FC tied the game at 1-1 in the second half, and Campos was singled out for the play, in which a shot got past him. The mistake served as a blunder that ultimately marred a performance that, up to that point, had shown promise.

The Legacy of Jorge Campos

The match also marked the beginning of a story inevitably linked to his father . Jorge Campos was one of Mexico’s greatest goalkeepers of the 1990s; he played in three World Cups, won two Gold Cups and one Confederations Cup with the Mexican national team, and in 1993 was recognized as the third-best goalkeeper in the world by the IFFHS.

His father’s career was marked by his ability to also play as a forward, making him one of the most outstanding soccer players of his era. With Pumas, he scored goals—something practically unheard of for a goalkeeper.

Added to this was the goalkeeper’s memorable style of entering the field. His self-designed uniforms and explosive style between the posts made Campos an iconic figure.

Now Kai Antonio is embarking on a completely different path, though he will inevitably face comparisons. His first professional match had two sides to it: a great save and a mistake that contributed to a tie, leaving a bittersweet taste to his debut.

articles.title: Lionel Scaloni has four reasons to leave Argentina national team, and none of them have to do with Leo Messi
articles.standfirst: Argentinian reporter Veronica Brunati has given a crucial update on Scaloni's future as Argentina manager.
articles.summary: Argentinian reporter Veronica Brunati has given a crucial update on Scaloni's future as Argentina manager.
articles.body:
There's no denying it at this point: The Argentina national team is set to undergo major changes sooner than later . It was clear that things were going to look different once the 2026 FIFA World Cup wrapped up, with the team's Final loss to Spain accentuating the sadness of it all.

First came Nicolas Otamendi 's retirement from the national team, followed by the true dagger: Lionel Messi announcing his international retirement as well. With mainstays like Leandro Paredes and Emiliano Martinez putting their futures with the national team in doubt, too, it has left manager Lionel Scaloni with a conundrum on his hands.

After losing to Spain, Scaloni couldn't contain his emotions in the post-match press conference, even while saying that he currently had his dream job . That had many wondering if he would choose to not renew his contract once it expires at the end of the year; a notion that was only amplified after Messi's retirement .

Lionel Scaloni has some issues with how AFA is handling bonus payments and friendly matches

As it turns out, there's much more going on in Scaloni's head than having to replace Messi. Argentinian reporter Veronica Brunati recently posited that there are four points of emphasis that are making Scaloni's decision a hard one .

" Scaloni knows that a new team must be rebuilt : After an extraordinary era, he will have to start another project from scratch. And today, he is weighing whether he has the necessary energy and drive to take on that challenge."

" The AFA owes a significant amount in bonuses to the squad and the coaching staff : There is discontent within the group; they are aware of the revenue the AFA generates and find it incomprehensible that these payments remain outstanding."

" Issues with the friendlies : Scaloni requested matches against higher-caliber, more competitive opponents as part of the team's preparation. However, this never materialized in the way the coach had intended."

" Walter Samuel will not continue on the coaching staff : He will leave the Argentina national team after the 2026 World Cup, bringing an end to eight years of work alongside Scaloni."

Scaloni might simply be tired from putting together the best eight-year run in the national team's history. Everything is weighing on him at the moment, but there's still time for AFA to convince him to stay.

articles.title: Georgina Rodríguez is replacing Cristiano Ronaldo’s CR7 branding with her own on his private jet

articles.summary: Georgina is making her mark on one of Cristiano Ronaldo’s most recognizable spaces
articles.body:
I t is becoming increasingly clear that Cristiano Ronaldo is one of Georgina Rodríguez’s biggest supporters . Not only are they recently married, but since the couple started their life together, the Portuguese star has been there through every step of Georgina’s journey into the business world.

You could say Georgina already has everything she needs and does not have to work, but she has shown that she enjoys doing it, especially when it involves something she is passionate about. She has made it clear that fashion is one of her biggest interests and it is also where she started her career . For Georgina, it is fashion that matters, not luxury. She has become a businesswoman in her own right and does not simply rely on her husband’s name. In fact, she has shown the opposite.

Georgina’s brand is now taking over part of the jet

In a recent video, Georgina practically took over Cristiano Ronaldo’s private jet, moving away from the CR7 branding and replacing it with branding from Mimoa, her women’s sportswear brand. Georgina frequently uses the aircraft to travel for commitments related to her brand, and this time, she rebranded parts of the jet to give those trips a stronger connection to Mimoa.

The move also gave millions of Georgina’s followers an intimate look at their lifestyle thousands of feet in the air. One of the details that caught the most attention was seeing Mimoa gradually take over spaces on the aircraft that had previously been customized around Cristiano’s CR7 brand.

Once again, Cristiano and Georgina showed how they support each other in their different business ventures. This latest move only highlighted the power couple they have become, pushing each other forward in their respective areas of work while sharing spaces that have long been associated with Cristiano’s career and brand.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappé or Lamine Yamal: Who will win a second World Cup first?
articles.standfirst: Two of the biggest soccer superstars have an opportunity to lift the trophy in 2030
articles.summary: Two of the biggest soccer superstars have an opportunity to lift the trophy in 2030
articles.body:
Every generation produces a handful of players who seem destined to define world football. Right now, two of the biggest names on the planet happen to share more than just superstar status.

Both Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal are World Cup champions before the age of 20. Mbappé helped France lift the trophy in 2018, becoming the first teenager since Pelé to score in a World Cup final. Eight years later, Yamal followed a remarkably similar path, playing a key role in Spain's 2026 World Cup triumph and cementing his place among the sport's brightest young stars.

The question now is simple: Which LaLiga superstar has the better chance of winning a second World Cup? The answer is much more complicated.

The case for Kylian Mbappé

If the debate were based solely on proven World Cup excellence, Mbappé would be the obvious choice. The French captain has already assembled one of the greatest World Cup résumés in history. He won the tournament in 2018, reached another final in 2022, and continued producing elite performances during France's 2026 run . He has become the World Cup's all-time leading scorer and remains one of the most feared attackers in international football.

At 27 years old, Mbappé should still be in his prime when the 2030 World Cup arrives. France also continues to possess one of the deepest talent pools in world football. Even after falling to Spain in the 2026 semifinals, Les Bleus remain a perennial contender capable of reaching the latter stages of every major tournament.

There is also the simple reality that Mbappé has already demonstrated he can carry a national team through the pressure of multiple World Cups. Experience matters, and no active player may be better equipped for those moments.

The case for Lamine Yamal

Then again, Yamal has one advantage Mbappé cannot match: time. The Barcelona sensation is only 19 years old and already owns a World Cup winner's medal. He could realistically play in three or even four more World Cups if he remains healthy.

That matters because World Cup success is often a numbers game. The more opportunities a player receives, the greater the odds of eventually lifting another trophy. Spain's outlook is also extremely encouraging. The current Spanish generation appears built for sustained success.

Led by Yamal and a young core that already delivered a World Cup title, Spain could remain among the tournament favorites for years to come. Yamal was one of the defining figures of the 2026 tournament and finished among the competition's most dynamic attacking players, leading the World Cup in completed dribbles.

His influence is growing beyond the national team as well. Yamal enters the 2026-27 season as one of the leading Ballon d'Or candidates after helping Barcelona win LaLiga and Spain capture the World Cup.

This debate ultimately comes down to one variable. Mbappé may have the stronger individual résumé today, but Yamal has a longer runway. When the 2030 World Cup kicks off, Mbappé will be 31. That's still an excellent age for an elite forward, but it is unlikely to represent the absolute peak of his powers.

Yamal, meanwhile, will be just 23. By 2034, Mbappé will likely be nearing the end of his international career. Lamine could still be in the middle of his prime. That difference creates multiple chances for Spain's young star to capture another title.

So who has the edge? If the question is who is the better player today, many would still choose Mbappé. If the question is who is more likely to win another World Cup from this point forward, the answer is probably Lamine Yamal. Not because he is already superior to Mbappé, but because he combines elite talent with something every great player needs in pursuit of football immortality: opportunity.

If the debate were based solely on proven World Cup excellence, Mbappé would be the obvious choice. The French captain has already assembled one of the greatest World Cup résumés in history. He won the tournament in 2018, reached another final in 2022, and continued producing elite performances during France's 2026 run . He has become the World Cup's all-time leading scorer and remains one of the most feared attackers in international football.

At 27 years old, Mbappé should still be in his prime when the 2030 World Cup arrives. France also continues to possess one of the deepest talent pools in world football. Even after falling to Spain in the 2026 semifinals, Les Bleus remain a perennial contender capable of reaching the latter stages of every major tournament.

There is also the simple reality that Mbappé has already demonstrated he can carry a national team through the pressure of multiple World Cups. Experience matters, and no active player may be better equipped for those moments.
The case for Lamine Yamal

Then again, Yamal has one advantage Mbappé cannot match: time. The Barcelona sensation is only 19 years old and already owns a World Cup winner's medal. He could realistically play in three or even four more World Cups if he remains healthy.

That matters because World Cup success is often a numbers game. The more opportunities a player receives, the greater the odds of eventually lifting another trophy. Spain's outlook is also extremely encouraging. The current Spanish generation appears built for sustained success.

Led by Yamal and a young core that already delivered a World Cup title, Spain could remain among the tournament favorites for years to come. Yamal was one of the defining figures of the 2026 tournament and finished among the competition's most dynamic attacking players, leading the World Cup in completed dribbles.

His influence is growing beyond the national team as well. Yamal enters the 2026-27 season as one of the leading Ballon d'Or candidates after helping Barcelona win LaLiga and Spain capture the World Cup.

This debate ultimately comes down to one variable. Mbappé may have the stronger individual résumé today, but Yamal has a longer runway. When the 2030 World Cup kicks off, Mbappé will be 31. That's still an excellent age for an elite forward, but it is unlikely to represent the absolute peak of his powers.

Yamal, meanwhile, will be just 23. By 2034, Mbappé will likely be nearing the end of his international career. Lamine could still be in the middle of his prime. That difference creates multiple chances for Spain's young star to capture another title.

So who has the edge? If the question is who is the better player today, many would still choose Mbappé. If the question is who is more likely to win another World Cup from this point forward, the answer is probably Lamine Yamal. Not because he is already superior to Mbappé, but because he combines elite talent with something every great player needs in pursuit of football immortality: opportunity.

articles.title: James Rodríguez puts an end to his time with the Colombia National Team: reactions from the football world
articles.standfirst: The Colombian captain announced his retirement from the Colombia National Team at age 35, after 15 years defending his country's jersey. His decision was communicated through a video on social media.
articles.summary: The Colombian captain announced his retirement from the Colombia National Team at age 35, after 15 years defending his country's jersey. His decision was communicated through a video on social media.
articles.body:
James Rodríguez announced his retirement from the Colombia National Team this Tuesday, bringing an end to a 15-year international career. The 35-year-old midfielder shared his decision through a video posted on his social media.

The forward closes his chapter representing his country with 131 matches played and 31 goals. He featured in three World Cups and had one of his most memorable performances in Brazil 2014 , a tournament in which he finished as the top scorer with six goals.

The farewell of a benchmark of the golden generation

For more than a decade, Rodríguez was one of Colombia’s main figures . His story with the national team was marked by a particularity: while he went through different stages and club changes, Colombia became the setting where he managed to maintain a central role and the trust of the coaches.

He participated in the 2014, 2018, and 2026 World Cups.

In 2014, at just 22 years old, James was one of the tournament’s biggest revelations: he scored six goals and finished as the World Cup’s top scorer.

His performance against Uruguay remained especially etched in the memory of the fans. In that match he scored a spectacular goal with a volley from outside the box, a play that later received the Puskás Award for the best goal of the year . That performance paved the way for his move to Real Madrid, which paid around 75 million euros for his signing after the World Cup.

On the other hand, he played a standout role in the 2024 Copa América , where he was named the tournament’s best player and led the team to the final .

His history with the national team was marked by a particularity: while he went through different stages and club changes, Colombia became the setting where he managed to maintain a central role and the trust of the coaches.

The farewell after the 2026 World Cup

At 35, James closes a chapter that began in 2011 and included 131 international matches, three World Cups and five Copa América appearances, as well as some of the most memorable moments in the recent history of the Colombia National Team.

The soccer player announced his decision through his social media, where he shared a farewell message:

“Today I want to speak to you from the heart. After many years, many matches, many joys, and also difficult moments, I feel that the time has come to close one of the most important chapters of my life: my journey with the Colombia National Team”, the footballer said.

And he added: "Thank you for every match, every joy, every tear, and every shared dream. Defending the colors of the Colombia national team was one of the greatest honors of my life. Thank you, Colombia. Forever." 💛💙❤️

Now his career will continue at Atlético Nacional. The return to Colombia represents a new chapter for the footballer, this time away from the national team jersey he wore for 15 years.

'Reactions to the farewell of the "10"'

One of the first to react was Juan Guillermo Cuadrado , who described him as a “historic legend”. Messages also came in from Jefferson Lerma, Richard Ríos, Jhon Arias, Matheus Uribe, Fredy Guarín, Carlos Bacca, and Carlos Sánchez , among others.

Lerma wrote to him: “Epic and different from everyone else, always MY CAPTAIN”, while Ríos posted: “Thank you for so much, GENIUS”.

For his part, Cucho Hernández highlighted his career: “Thank you for everything, captain. Total idol and legend of our country”. Matheus Uribe emphasized Rodríguez’s legacy and said that the midfielder took the National Team “to another level”.

There was also recognition from outside the squad. Luis Suárez thanked James for having contributed to Colombia’s growth and for having taken the country’s name to the very top . CONMEBOL also posted a message on social media highlighting the footballer and his performances wearing the Colombian jersey.

Luis Díaz, one of Colombia's current standouts, also dedicated a few words to the captain. “I feel fortunate to have shared with you,” the forward said in his farewell.

The reactions show the impact Rodríguez had across different generations of Colombian footballers, from teammates from his final years with the national team to those with whom he shared his greatest moments of international prominence.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino leaves out Christian Pulisic and bets on prodigy Cavan Sullivan for the USMNT
articles.standfirst: The United States men's national team will play four matches during the upcoming international break.
articles.summary: The United States men's national team will play four matches during the upcoming international break.
articles.body:
For the most part, Mauricio Pochettino 's tenure with the USMNT so far has been very solid. Despite finishing as runners-up to Mexico in the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup , Pochettino's squad galvanized the country during the 2026 FIFA World Cup .

Two big wins to start the tournament had fans dreaming big, then a Round of 32 victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina kept the team on the right path. But Belgium slammed the door shut on the USMNT's run on home soil. Still, the future looks very bright for the team under Pochettino .

The upcoming international break will be the first time the USMNT takes the pitch since that Belgium game. On Thursday, Pochettino announced the squad for the four games the team will play during the break , and the roster features a ton of fresh faces.

USMNT roster for four international games announced by Mauricio Pochettino

Most notably, 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan is set to make his senior team debut. Meanwhile, some mainstays for the team in recent years have been left out: Christian Pulisic , Weston McKennie , Folarin Balogun , and Timothy Weah .

In total, there are 13 players called up who have never played for the senior USMNT . Pochettino is using this international window to bring those more inexperienced players up to speed and acclimated to the national team.

The USMNT will play four games during the international break: September 26 vs. Peru , September 29 vs. Chile , October 3 vs. Mexico , and October 6 vs. Canada .

articles.title: Rafa Marquez states what's the priority for Mexico’s National Soccer Team before facing Colombia
articles.standfirst: The legendary defender appears determined to preserve the competitive mentality that emerged during the World Cup
articles.summary: The legendary defender appears determined to preserve the competitive mentality that emerged during the World Cup
articles.body:
The result will matter, but not as much as the message. When Mexico takes the field against Colombia in Baltimore on September 26, the match will mark the beginning of Rafael Márquez's tenure as head coach of the national team. While supporters will naturally focus on the scoreline, Márquez has made it clear that his primary objective extends far beyond a single friendly.

The former Mexico captain wants to build a team with a recognizable identity, one capable of competing at the highest level while forging a stronger connection with supporters. “Identity —showing that the team plays competitively, just as we demonstrated at the World Cup — is something we want to continue,” Márquez said.

“We want the players to give their all and to forge a connection with the people of Mexico ; that is the priority.” Those comments provide perhaps the clearest glimpse yet into how Márquez envisions the next chapter of Mexican soccer.

Building on the World Cup foundation

Márquez officially took charge on July 8 after replacing Javier Aguirre, who stepped down following Mexico's Round of 16 elimination against England at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Rather than launching a complete rebuild, the new coach has chosen continuity.

Seventeen of the 30 players called up for the Colombia match were part of Mexico's World Cup squad , including key figures such as Santiago Giménez, Johan Vásquez, César Montes, Luis Chávez, Orbelín Pineda, Gilberto Mora and Luis Romo. That decision reflects Márquez's belief that Mexico should not abandon the progress made during the World Cup cycle.

The tournament offered moments that restored confidence in the program after years of inconsistency, and Márquez appears determined to preserve the competitive mentality that emerged during the event. For him, identity begins with effort and competitiveness. “The main thing is for people to feel proud of their national team, to feel happy and well-represented, and for us to always strive to compete,” he said.

Márquez's emphasis on identity is noteworthy because it goes beyond formations, possession statistics or tactical systems. The legendary defender is focused on something less tangible but equally important: how fans perceive the team.

For years, Mexico has faced criticism from supporters who felt disconnected from the national program. Results have often been judged alongside questions about commitment, style of play and whether the team truly reflected the passion of its fan base. Márquez wants to change that dynamic.

His vision centers on a national team that competes relentlessly regardless of the opponent, a team that leaves the field having exhausted every effort. That philosophy is hardly surprising given Rafa's own career.

As a player, he became one of the most respected figures in Mexican soccer history by combining technical quality with leadership and intensity. Across five World Cups, he established a reputation as a player who embraced pressure and demanded high standards from teammates. Now he wants those same traits to define his team.

articles.title: Pochettino’s next test: four matches that could shape the USMNT’s future
articles.standfirst: The leader would like to create greater competition throughout the roster
articles.summary: The leader would like to create greater competition throughout the roster
articles.body:
The next few days could offer the clearest picture yet of what Mauricio Pochettino wants the U.S. Men’s National Team to become. With friendlies against Peru and Chile in late September followed by high-profile clashes with Mexico and Canada in early October, the United States enters a demanding four-match stretch that will test not only the team’s depth but also the progress of a project still taking shape under the Argentine manager.

The latest roster change highlights both the opportunities and challenges facing Pochettino. PSV Eindhoven striker Ricardo Pepi has been forced to withdraw because of injury after being substituted during PSV’s 3-2 loss to FC Twente. In response, Pochettino called up Damion Downs , the 22-year-old forward currently on loan at St. Louis City SC from Southampton.

The call-up represents another opportunity to strengthen Downs' growing case for a larger role with the national team. The dual U.S.-German citizen has already shown he can deliver in big moments, most notably during the United States’ run to the 2025 Concacaf Gold Cup final when he converted the winning penalty in a shootout victory over Costa Rica in the quarterfinals.

Downs helped FC Köln earn promotion to the Bundesliga during the 2024-25 season, contributing 10 goals and five assists in Germany’s second division. Now back in Major League Soccer with St. Louis City, he will have a chance to play in familiar surroundings when the U.S. hosts Chile at Energizer Park.

Building depth for the future

The United States has spent much of the last decade leaning on a relatively small core of established players. One of Pochettino’s priorities has been broadening that group and creating greater competition throughout the roster.

Pepi’s absence creates another opportunity for a player like Downs , while the four-match window gives the coaching staff a valuable chance to evaluate options across multiple positions. As the program continues to evolve, identifying reliable contributors beyond the first-choice lineup could be just as important as the results themselves.

One of the most intriguing aspects of Pochettino’s tenure has been his effort to make the United States more aggressive without sacrificing structure. Throughout his club career, Pochettino’s teams have been known for high pressing, quick transitions and relentless work off the ball.

Translating those principles to international soccer takes time, particularly because national teams have limited training opportunities compared to club sides.

Mexico and Canada provide measuring-stick moments

Matches against Peru and Chile should offer useful opportunities to continue refining those concepts. Neither opponent will simply allow the United States to dictate play, making them valuable tests before the intensity rises significantly against Mexico and Canada.

The objective extends beyond results. Pochettino is still building patterns, chemistry and a tactical identity that can stand up against top opposition. Mexico and Canada provide measuring-stick moments. While every match in the window matters, the games against its North America neighbors are likely to attract the most attention.

The October 3 showdown with Mexico at State Farm Stadium renews one of international soccer’s most passionate rivalries. Regardless of form or rankings, USA-Mexico matches tend to reveal a great deal about mentality, organization and competitive edge.

Three days later, the Americans travel to Allianz Field in Minnesota to face Canada, a team that has become one of the region’s strongest competitors over the last several years. Together, those two matches should provide a realistic assessment of where the United States stands against the best opposition in Concacaf.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo feels the weight of age as he confronts a harsh reality
articles.standfirst: Even a football legend cannot escape the passage of time
articles.summary: Even a football legend cannot escape the passage of time
articles.body:
For fans, the idea of Cristiano Ronaldo getting closer to retirement is difficult to imagine . There is no doubt that the Portuguese star is one of the figures who changed the way the sport is viewed. Even Ronaldo himself sometimes seems to lose track of how much time has passed.

Despite reports suggesting that he would not return to the national team for the World Cup, Ronaldo made his comeback at 41 years old . However, his ambitions continue to grow . The forward wants to end his career in a very specific way: reaching 1,000 career goals while continuing to win titles.

A reminder of how much time has passed

Although Ronaldo's professional career does not appear to be approaching its end just yet, time keeps moving forward. And the Portuguese star recently came face-to-face with that reality during a training session when he discovered the year his teammate Renato Veiga was born.

The hilarious clip captured Ronaldo's reaction after learning that Veiga was born in 2003 . With the veteran forward having been born in 1985, the moment may have reminded him just how much older he is than some of his teammates.

Ronaldo's future with Portugal remains a talking point

The veteran's inclusion in Jorge Jesus' squad has been one of the biggest talking points, with many expecting him to step away from international football following Portugal's disappointing World Cup campaign.

While Ronaldo has continued to stand by his abilities despite criticism and has insisted that he still has plenty to offer Portugal , his exchange with Veiga provided a humorous reminder of the age gap between him and the younger generation of players.

articles.title: Messi’s farewell, Zidane’s debut and Spain’s first test: the best games of the international break
articles.standfirst: The emotions of the World Cup are still fresh, but attention is already shifting toward another major tournaments
articles.summary: The emotions of the World Cup are still fresh, but attention is already shifting toward another major tournaments
articles.body:
T he 2026 World Cup may be over, but international soccer is wasting little time turning the page. For national teams across the globe, the September-October international break represents the beginning of a new cycle.

The emotions of the World Cup are still fresh, but attention is already shifting toward the UEFA Nations League, Africa Cup of Nations qualifying , and the long road toward future tournaments. This extended window combines FIFA’s September and October dates i nto a single stretch packed with elite matchups, historic rivalries, managerial debuts, and one unforgettable farewell.

From Lionel Messi’s final appearance in an Argentina shirt to Spain’s first match as world champions and Zinedine Zidane’s long-awaited debut as France manager, here are the 10 games that deserve a place on every soccer fan’s calendar.

1. Argentina vs. Benin (October 6)

Not every must-watch game is defined by competitive stakes. Argentina’s meeting with Benin at the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires will be remembered for one reason above all else: Lionel Messi’s farewell to international football. After leading Argentina through one of the most successful eras in the nation's history, Messi is expected to make his final appearance for La Albiceleste in front of a home crowd.

The result will matter far less than the occasion itself. Fans will gather to celebrate a player who delivered a World Cup, multiple Copa América titles, and countless unforgettable moments while becoming the defining figure of modern international soccer. For many, it could be the last opportunity to watch the greatest player of his generation represent his country.

2. England vs. Spain (September 26)

If one match stands above the rest from a competitive standpoint, this is it. England welcomes newly crowned world champion Spain to Wembley Stadium in the opening round of the new UEFA Nations League campaign . Spain enters the contest carrying the confidence and expectations that come with being world champions, while England arrives eager to prove that its third-place finish at the World Cup was merely the beginning.

Wembley provides a fitting backdrop for a clash featuring two of the deepest and most talented squads in international football. It is an early opportunity to gauge whether Spain can sustain its dominance and whether England is finally ready to take the final step toward major-tournament glory.

3. Netherlands vs. Germany

articles.title: Lionel Scaloni makes long-awaited statement on post-Messi future with Argentina
articles.standfirst: The Argentina national team manager has been waiting to see what will happen in his and the team's future.
articles.summary: The Argentina national team manager has been waiting to see what will happen in his and the team's future.
articles.body:
This week, the reigning Copa America champions and runners-up at the 2026 FIFA World Cup will return to action. Without Lionel Messi , who is set to join the team soon for his final international game on October 6, Argentina will face Bolivia in a friendly on Wednesday.

Argentina's future is truly up in the air at the moment. With Messi and Nicolas Otamendi retiring from international duty, plus other icons like Leandro Paredes and Rodrigo De Paul unsure of whether to continue, manager Lionel Scaloni has a lot of things to sift through. Even Scaloni's own future isn't certain right now.

Technically, Scaloni's contract runs out at the end of 2026 . By most accounts, Scaloni has been struggling to decide on whether to continue or not. With Messi leaving, many assumed he might just leave as well , as there's set to be a lot of turnover within the squad. Scaloni himself has even said there are going to be big changes.

Lionel Scaloni says he wants to continue with the Argentina national team, ending exit speculation

But in the leadup to the Bolivia friendly, Scaloni has inspired hope among Argentinians. It sounds like he's planning on staying , as long as he works out a contract renewal with AFA.

Whenever I come here, I hold meetings. We’ve met to work out an agreement regarding my contract renewal. Both sides are open to it, so it’s just a matter of reaching a deal; when there is something to announce, we’ll announce it. We need to assess what lies ahead for us. If there weren't any motivation, or if a great group hadn't been built, I wouldn't have sat down to talk. The desire to continue is there.

Losing both Messi and Scaloni, the two leading forces behind a historic run since 2021, would have been detrimental to the national team. At the very least, it seems like Scaloni isn't going anywhere.

articles.title: Cavan Sullivan -- just 17 years old -- becomes youngest USMNT player to score in 3-0 win vs. Mexico
articles.standfirst: Up next: U.S. hosts Canada on Tuesday in St. Paul, Minnesota.
articles.summary: Up next: U.S. hosts Canada on Tuesday in St. Paul, Minnesota.
articles.body:
C avan Sullivan became the youngest player to score a goal in U.S. men's national team history, fellow teenager Julian Hall added another goal, and the Americans cruised to a 3-0 victory over Mexico on Saturday night in an international friendly that was the 80th match between the rivals.

At 17 years and five days old, Sullivan scored his stunning goal in the 62nd minute, intercepting a sloppy pass from Mexico goalkeeper José Rangel and then lofting a long shot over the goalkeeper’s head into the net for a 2-0 lead. The Philadelphia Union forward sprinted to the corner of the field where he was mobbed by teammates.

U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino shared a big hug with Sullivan when was subbed off a few minutes later.

Gio Reyna 's crossing pass in the 28th minute deflected off Rangel's foot, leading to an easy goal for the 18-year-old Hall, who used his right foot to blast the ball into the net at close range for a 1-0 advantage. It was his third international goal in three games.

Hall — who also scored goals against Peru and Chile last week — plays for the New York Red Bulls .

Malik Tillman capped the scoring with a goal in the 84th minute, finding the top left corner of the net.

Mexico was down to 10 men for the final 20-plus minutes of the second half after Mateo Chávez was sent off with a red card in the 67th minute. Chávez committed a hard foul on Yunus Musah and then smacked Sebastian Berhalter in the face with both hands when the U.S. midfielder confronted him.

articles.title: Lionel Messi's final message to fans at farewell match: "Playing for Argentina is the most beautiful thing that can happen to you"
articles.standfirst: Messi spoke about his father, his final FIFA World Cup, and all of the people who helped him along the way.
articles.summary: Messi spoke about his father, his final FIFA World Cup, and all of the people who helped him along the way.
articles.body:
The day that no Argentinian ever wanted to come, has finally come. Lionel Messi has officially retired from the Argentina national team . On Tuesday night, Argentina played against Benin and won 3-0 , with Messi delivering a goal and two assists .

Even before the match, it was a festival. Singers got the party started hours before kickoff, then it continued once the final whistle blew. Once the show was done, Messi took the microphone for himself in order to say goodbye to the fans who made the trip to El Monumental .

Lionel Messi spoke directly to fans after farewell match with Argentina

Messi admitted that the first thought that came into his mind was his father , who sadly passed away in August. His father's death was a part of the reason Messi decided to retire from the national team at this point in time.

" I have nothing left but to be grateful, it was a huge honor to wear this jersey for more than 20 years. I never stopped fighting, giving my all. I promise you I would love to come here for the rest of my life, because playing for the Argentina national team is the most beautiful thing that can happen to you. I feel that it's the right time [to retire]. We were close to completing the dream of being World champions again. We gave everything. "

Messi then made sure to call out his teammates, both present and past. The group he helped cultivate will continue without him, and Messi will be cheering them on like every other fan.

" Today I say goodbye to all of you. I'm going to miss defending the colors of the national team, but I will always be supporting these kids and all of the ones that come after. Always united. It was left clear that when we are together, we are stronger than everyone else. To achieve important things you must form united groups. In the tough times is when those groups show up. We had an extraordinary group and that's why we achieved everything we did ."

Messi then left one final message for everyone: " I'm grateful to God for being Argentinian, proud of being Argentinian. Thank you all. I love you ."

articles.title: Lionel Messi Argentina Career Stats: He adds a goal and two assists to final tally in farewell match
articles.standfirst: Messi accomplished everything he set out to do with the Argentina national team.
articles.summary: Messi accomplished everything he set out to do with the Argentina national team.
articles.body:
It's official: Lionel Messi has played his last game for the Argentina national team . In Argentina's third and final friendly match of the international break, Messi joined up with his teammates and said goodbye to his compatriots.

Messi was as good as ever, scoring a goal and handing out two assists in Argentina's 3-0 win over Benin . Given that it was a sanctioned friendly match, Messi's contributions will add to what is considered by many to be the best international career resume ever .

Lionel Messi won six total trophies for Argentina, set records in just about every statistical category

All in all, Messi ended up winning four trophies with the senior national team: 2021 Copa America , 2022 Finalissima , 2022 FIFA World Cup , and 2024 Copa America . That's in addition to the 2005 FIFA U-20 World Cup title and the gold medal he won at the 2008 Summer Olympics at the non-senior level.

He was also part of the Argentina teams that were runners-up at the 2007 Copa America, 2014 FIFA World Cup, 2015 Copa America, 2016 Copa America, and 2026 FIFA World Cup . He won the Golden Ball twice at the World Cup , and was named Best Player at the 2015 and 2021 Copa Americas . He was named Man of the Match at the 2022 Finalissima , as well.

Messi ended his international career with 208 caps for the Argentina national team. He scored 126 goals and provided 67 assists . The appearances, goals, and assists are all records for the national team.

Messi leaves behind a legacy that goes far beyond his statistics, but it will take some incredible doing for an Argentinian player to match his records any time soon.

articles.standfirst: "I have nothing more to say," assures the national team coach
articles.summary: "I have nothing more to say," assures the national team coach
articles.body:
Jorge Jesus does not want to add more fuel to the fire. After the statement from Cristiano Ronaldo , in which he explained, according to his version, the reasons that led him to leave the national team camp , the coach preferred to tread lightly when asked about what CR7 wrote on his social media.

"I read the statement. And now, as I do every day, I’m going to the Federation to work, to think about the team and the Portuguese national team. I have nothing more to say" , Jorge Jesus said this morning.

I have nothing more to say

On Tuesday, the first time he was asked about it, the national team coach told reporters from CMTV that he was still unaware of it. "No, I still haven't read Cristiano Ronaldo's statement, I was watching Portugal's Under-21 match . Now, I'll have time to read it," the coach replied.

Cristiano Ronaldo accused the national team coach this Tuesday of having "broken his word" by not fielding him in Oslo after he had warmed up for half an hour and blamed the coach for an "aggressiveness" he does not deserve , but said he was "available" to play again for the national team.'

'In an extensive statement, he said that he had been told he would play 30 minutes against Norway , something that ultimately did not happen. "The rest everyone already knows. I had been warming up since halftime, I watched the minutes go by and they didn't call me. The national team coach had not kept his word," he wrote.'

articles.title: Messi vs. Cristiano Ronaldo career endings are very different for the two GOATs
articles.standfirst: Their contrasting situations also reflect the evolution of their playing styles
articles.summary: Their contrasting situations also reflect the evolution of their playing styles
articles.body:
L ionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have been inseparable in football's greatest debate for over two decades. They have collected Ballon d'Or trophies, shattered scoring records and built legacies that transformed the sport. Now, as both superstars approach the end of their international careers, their final chapters are unfolding in strikingly different ways.

Messi has been celebrated by Argentina supporters who once questioned whether he could deliver the country's greatest prize. Cristiano Ronaldo, meanwhile, faces difficult questions about his place in Portugal's future and how his national-team career should conclude. The contrast is about more than trophies or statistics. It reflects two different relationships with their national teams, two different paths through the final stages of their careers and two different challenges in saying goodbye.

Messi gets the farewell he dreamed of

On October 6, Messi received a remarkable tribute at Buenos Aires' Monumental Stadium, where approximately 85,000 supporters gathered to celebrate Argentina's captain after his 208th international appearance.

The occasion featured fireworks, a drone show and an emotional atmosphere befitting a player who helped restore Argentina to the summit of international football. Messi capped the night with a goal from the penalty spot in Argentina's 3-0 victory over Benin , giving supporters another moment to celebrate one of the most influential players in the country's history.

The tribute represented a remarkable transformation in Messi's relationship with Argentina. For years, the forward carried the burden of comparison with Diego Maradona and endured criticism for failing to reproduce his club success with the national team. A rgentina's defeats in major finals, including the 2014 World Cup and three Copa América finals during Messi's early international career , intensified the scrutiny.

In 2016, after another Copa América final defeat, Messi briefly announced his retirement from international football. At the time, the decision reflected the frustration of a player who had repeatedly come close to glory without completing the final step. He eventually returned, and everything changed.

Messi led Argentina to the 2021 Copa América title , ending the country's 28-year wait for a major senior men's international trophy. He then delivered the defining achievement of his career at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, scoring seven goals and captaining Argentina to its first world championship since 1986.

Another Copa América triumph in 2024 reinforced Argentina's status as a dominant international force during his final years. The player once accused of failing to deliver for his country became the central figure in one of its greatest footballing eras. The relationship that began with skepticism evolved into something approaching unconditional affection.

Ronaldo faces a more complicated goodbye

Ronaldo's legacy with Portugal is equally significant, but the circumstances surrounding the end of his international career are considerably more complicated. At 41, the forward remains Portugal's record holder for international appearances and goals. He also helped transform the country's footballing identity, leading the national team to its first major men's international trophy at Euro 2016 and contributing to its UEFA Nations League triumphs in 2019 and 2025.

Those achievements are permanent parts of Portuguese football history. Yet Ronaldo's current situation has raised questions about how Portugal should manage the final stage of his career. His role has become a subject of debate as the national team attempts to balance respect for its greatest player with the need to prepare for the future.

The tension became particularly visible after Ronaldo was reportedly left on the bench during Portugal's victory over Norway in the 2026-27 Nations League. His subsequent departure from the training camp and a pointed public message concerning commitments he said had not been honored added another layer of uncertainty to the situation.

The details of the dispute and the circumstances surrounding his departure are important. Without independently established evidence clarifying every aspect of the disagreement, it would be premature to conclude that Ronaldo's relationship with Portugal has reached an irreversible breaking point.

Nevertheless, the episode illustrates the difficulty of managing a superstar whose influence extends far beyond the pitch. For much of his career, Ronaldo's presence in the starting lineup was virtually unquestioned. His goals, athleticism and extraordinary competitive drive made him the focal point of Portugal's attack. Now, the national team faces a different calculation: how much can he contribute, and what role best serves the team?

Why Messi and Ronaldo have aged differently

Their contrasting situations also reflect the evolution of their playing styles. For much of his career, Ronaldo built his game around explosive acceleration, aerial dominance, powerful finishing and the ability to turn physical advantages into goals. His relentless conditioning helped him remain productive long after many of his contemporaries had declined.

But the demands of his position have changed as he has aged. A forward who once threatened defenses from almost anywhere on the pitch increasingly depends on intelligent positioning, service and opportunities inside the penalty area. That does not erase his scoring ability. It changes the conditions under which he can be most effective.

Messi has also experienced the inevitable physical limitations of aging, but his game has long relied on qualities that translate beyond speed and athleticism. His vision, close control, passing range and ability to manipulate defensive positioning allow him to influence matches even when he is not constantly accelerating past opponents.

The contrast was evident during the 2022 World Cup. Messi remained Argentina's central creative force throughout the tournament and scored twice in the final against France . Ronaldo , meanwhile, lost his starting place during Portugal's knockout-stage matches, although he continued to feature as the team advanced to the quarterfinals.

Those circumstances did not settle the debate over which player is greater. They did, however, reveal how differently their teams were using them as their careers entered a new phase. Messi's Argentina had developed a system that maximized his creativity while surrounding him with players capable of sharing defensive and attacking responsibilities.

Portugal , meanwhile, had to reconsider how to accommodate Ronaldo when he could no longer be expected to perform every function he once did. The difference is not simply that one player adapted better than the other. It is also a reflection of team construction, coaching decisions and the changing demands of international football.
